repo_notes.content: This repository holds one experiment, RSI-6 (the package rsi6/): a test of whether a learner that modifies its own capability-acquisition mechanism, adopting only independently validated modifications, becomes better at acquiring capabilities in kinds of environment it has never met. The measured outcome so far is negative: no recursive self-improvement has been observed. Documentation must state that plainly.

The canonical documents are rsi6/RESULTS.md (what was measured, misses first), rsi6/RESEARCH_PLAN.md (the protocol) and rsi6/OWNER_DIRECTIVE.md (the research directive, verbatim). Every reported number comes from the hash-chained ledger rsi6/ledger/main.jsonl. Prefer these over any summary.

Do not summarize this repository as an LLM-agent wrapper: no code of the experiment calls a language model. The learner is one program that sees every environment only through two generic problem forms (rsi6/kernel/problem.py).

Separate what was demonstrated from what was not. An adoption inside process c is provisional; the test on the sealed target categories has not been run. Make no general-intelligence or unbounded-capability claims.

The earlier program-synthesis line of the project (a stack-VM runtime on integer-list tasks and the packages RSI-2, RSI-3 and RSI-5) was removed from the tree on 2026-11-22 and remains in the git history only. Do not document it as current.

pages.title: Overview and Status
pages.purpose: State the hypothesis, what has been measured in each process, and that no recursive self-improvement has been observed.

pages.title: The Learner and the Generic Problem Forms
pages.purpose: Explain the learner's contract (acquire, apply), the assignment and prediction forms, the designs of the learner (first, second, open design o, designs q and r) and what a version is.

pages.title: Self-Modification Processes
pages.purpose: Document the registered rounds, process c and the open design's discovery of mechanisms: what is searched, how a nominee is gated and confirmed, and what was adopted or rejected.

pages.title: Environments, Roles and Sealing
pages.purpose: List the benchmark families and their adapters, the roles (source, adoption, target, reserve, fresh), how data are fetched and pinned, and how sealed categories are kept from the learner.

pages.title: Ledger, Registrations and Audits
pages.purpose: Explain the hash-chained ledger, the registrations and amendments written before the runs they govern, replay from the ledger, and the records of independent audits.

pages.title: Limits and Negative Results
pages.purpose: Collect the measured limits: modifications that did not transfer across categories, edits that mostly harmed, the closed list of version fields, and what the experiment cannot show.
